the_span_guard.note: the one piece of non-trivial control flow in the body, and every step of it is an instruction
the_span_guard.0x00ecc643: SUB ECX,EAX -- the distance from +0x80 to +0x88, as a 32-bit subtraction that WRAPS. A negative distance is representable and is not special-cased anywhere.
the_span_guard.0x00ecc645: AND ECX,0xfffffffe -- clears bit 0, so the compared quantity is always even. This is what makes the constant 2 usable as a 'more than one element' test.
the_span_guard.0x00ecc64b: JLE 0x00ecc65a -- a SIGNED less-or-equal, so the body proceeds only when the masked distance is a signed value strictly greater than two. The signedness is load-bearing: masked values with bit 31 set are enormous unsigned and negative signed, and are rejected.
the_span_guard.0x00ecc64d: TEST EAX,EAX -- the SECOND guard, on the BEGIN word and not on the distance.
the_span_guard.0x00ecc64f: JE 0x00ecc65a -- a null begin is skipped even when the span test passed. The two guards are independent; neither implies the other, and the model test drives both halves of each.

boundary_table.3: masked 2, rejected -- the mask makes 3 indistinguishable from 2, and this is the off-by-one the test aims at
boundary_table.4: masked 4, ACCEPTED -- the first accepted value
boundary_table.0x7fffffff: masked 0x7ffffffe, accepted -- the largest accepted value
boundary_table.0x80000000: masked 0x80000000, rejected as a negative signed value

unresolved_questions: What the two words at receiver+0x80 and +0x88 actually are. The body only subtracts and masks them, and this package therefore claims nothing about their type beyond being 32-bit words at those two displacements. Three facts constrain but do not settle it: the constructor initialises them 0x01667bac and 0x01667bae, a two-byte run; 0x00ecc550 passes &receiver+0x80 to a virtual function taken from the table's slot +0x40, so +0x80 is the address of a subobject; and 0x00ecc530 compares +0x80 against +0x84, so the third word in that region is distinct from both. Whether the run is a byte buffer, a null-terminated string, a pointer range or a small inline vector is not established by any record in this repository.

Why the guard's threshold is 2 rather than any other constant. The mask-then-compare pair behaves exactly as an MSVC 'more than one element, so the storage is heap and must be released' test, and 0x00642190 runs the identical idiom on its own pair, but no record states the intent and the unit (bytes, elements, words) is not fixed by any instruction.

Whether the deallocation of the +0x80 run and the deallocation of the object are always the same allocator. Both go through 0x00f47380 in this body, but the constructor does not allocate that run (it points it at a static-looking address) and whatever installs a heap run on it is not identified here. Whether some other port is used elsewhere in the class is not established.
